criteria.statement: Every AC has at least one test case, every test case names its AC, and any AC without a case is listed as a gap (unmapped_requirements or test_gaps).

anchors.0: At least one AC has no test case and is not listed as a gap anywhere.
anchors.1: Every AC is either covered or listed as a gap, but at least one test case names no AC or names an AC that does not exist.
anchors.2: Complete and every case names its AC; one inconsistency between the cases document and the mapping (e.g. a TC in the mapping that is not in the document).
anchors.3: Complete, every case names its AC, the mapping and the document agree exactly, and gaps are listed by AC.

criteria.statement: coverage is "full" only where a happy path, a negative case and (where applicable) a boundary case exist for that AC; otherwise it is "partial" with the gap named, or "none".

anchors.0: "full" is claimed for an AC that has only a happy-path case, or "none" is used where cases exist.
anchors.1: Coverage values are mostly right but at least one "partial" has no gap named in test_gaps.
anchors.2: Every coverage value is justified by the cases; one AC could be argued either way and the choice is not explained.
anchors.3: Every coverage value is justified by the listed cases and every "partial" names its gap.

criteria.statement: The test cases document contains no fenced code; automation constraints go into Preconditions as prose.

An existing automated test is credited as covering an AC only with the file and the assertion that would fail if that AC broke; a test whose assertion cannot fail for the AC is not credited (judge notes name any such test).

anchors.0: A test the judge notes identify as vacuous is credited as coverage.
anchors.1: No vacuous test is credited, but a credit names only a file or a test title, not the failing assertion.
anchors.2: Every credit names file and assertion; one credited assertion is arguably weaker than the AC requires.
anchors.3: Every credit names file and the assertion that would fail, and every vacuous test in the judge notes is listed as a gap instead — or no existing test covers any AC and none is credited.

criteria.statement: P0 cases are at most half of all cases and at least one P0 covers the core happy path; case count is proportional to the ACs (no padding).

anchors.0: More than half the cases are P0, or the core happy path has no P0.
anchors.1: Distribution is within bounds but several cases are padding (restate another case with a trivial variation).
anchors.2: Distribution is within bounds and cases are distinct; one priority is debatable.
anchors.3: Distribution is within bounds, cases are distinct, and priorities follow the P0/P1/P2 rules in Phase 2 exactly.

criteria.statement: Every precondition or step that names a control label, a seeded record, a displayed value or a request is backed by an Observed: line in the scratchpad or carries (unverified).

anchors.0: A step names a label or record that does not exist in the app (judge notes list the real ones) and carries no (unverified).
anchors.1: Named details are real but none is backed by an Observed: line and none is marked (unverified).
anchors.2: Named details are backed by Observed: lines or marked (unverified), with at most one omission.
anchors.3: Every named detail is either observed or marked (unverified), and unreachable-app runs mark every dependent step.

criteria.statement: The run's scratchpad records what was observed, or records that the app was unreachable.
At least one reference section or learning was cited via `log applied` during the run (preamble obligation 2).
The test cases document ends with the Status / Summary / Next steps block.
